chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Hammad from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) while we were in Medina about the preparation for Ihram, so he said: 'Look around in Medina and equip yourself with whatever you wish, and perform Ghusl, and if you wish, enjoy the use of your Qamis (shirt) until you reach Masjid al-Shajara.'

key_terms.اِسْتَمْتَعْتَ بِقَمِيصِكَ: Enjoy the use of your shirt (wearing sewn garments)
key_terms.مَسْجِدَ اَلشَّجَرَةِ: Masjid al-Shajara (the specific boundary in Medina)

ai.seo_question: What are the ritual preparations for Ihram in Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the practical flexibility in the Hanafi and Shia jurisprudence regarding the boundary of Ihram, specifically identifying Masjid al-Shajara as the Miqat for residents of Medina. The Imam’s instruction to 'enjoy your shirt' until reaching this landmark underscores the permissibility of wearing sewn garments (Qamis) prior to the designated station, emphasizing a gradual transition into the sacred state rather than an abrupt change. This reflects the broader Shia scholarly emphasis on ease (Yusr) in ritual preparation while maintaining strict adherence to the physical markers of sanctity.
